commands.description: Creates a document in a workspace, optionally under a parent and with an initial Markdown body. Without afterId/beforeId it is appended as the last child.

flags.name: teamspace-id
flags.description: Hosted: the teamspace a top-level page goes into (null: the creator's private section; absent: the workspace's default teamspace, which every member shares). Ignored for child pages, which share their parent's space, and in local mode.

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key. Overrides afterId/beforeId; recorded by clients so replays converge.

commands.description: Moves a document (and its subtree) under a new parent, or to the top level with parentId null. Without afterId/beforeId it becomes the last child.

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key. Overrides afterId/beforeId; recorded by clients so replays converge.

commands.description: Soft-deletes a document and its subtree. Restore it with doc.restore. Deleting a deleted document is a no-op.
Restores a soft-deleted document and the part of its subtree deleted with it. If its parent is gone it is restored to the top level.
Permanently deletes a document in the trash, its trashed subtree, bodies and outgoing links. Links to it become unresolved. Cannot be undone.
Merges `set` into the document's properties and removes the keys in `unset`.

Changes a document's title, properties and body in one step, all or nothing; pass any of them. properties is merged into the document's properties and unset removes keys; on a database row they are its values, keyed by property id, key or name and checked like write_database_rows. markdown replaces the body, or edits are applied in order: replace swaps oldStr for newStr, insertBefore/insertAfter put newStr next to oldStr, prepend/append add newStr as a block at the start/end. oldStr is matched against the Markdown from fetch_doc and must occur exactly once unless replaceAll. expectedVersion (from fetch_doc) makes a stale body write a conflict.

flags.name: markdown
flags.description: The new body as Lydie Markdown.

commands.description: Replaces the body with markdown, or applies edits in order, all or nothing: replace swaps oldStr for newStr, insertBefore/insertAfter put newStr next to oldStr, prepend/append add newStr as a block at the start/end (also of an empty body). oldStr is matched against the Markdown from fetch_doc and must occur exactly once unless replaceAll; otherwise nothing is written and the error names the edit. expectedVersion makes a stale write a conflict.
Returns a document's metadata and, unless includeBody is false, its Markdown body, with `threads`: the open notes and comments left beside it, when there are any.
Lists documents depth-first in tree order. With rootId, lists that document's descendants only.
Lists the direct children of a document (or the top level when parentId is omitted) in order, each with its number of live children. Use it to load a tree level by level.

Full-text search over titles and bodies. Words are matched as prefixes; all words must match. A title equal to the query comes first. When nothing matches, titles similar to the query (sharing most of its letter trigrams, so typos still find them) are returned instead, without <mark> highlights.
Lists live documents that link to this document.
Lists live documents that link to one block (`[[Note#^blockId]]`) of this document.
Lists the links in this document (body first, then properties, in document order), each with the live document it resolves to or null.
Lists live documents whose text mentions this document's title without linking to it.
Lists links in live documents whose target does not exist (yet).
Lists saved versions of a document's body, newest first.
Returns one saved version of a document's body as Markdown.
Makes the body read as a saved version again, as a new edit. The body before the restore is kept as a version (`previousVersionId`): restore it to undo.
Lists what is in a workspace's trash, newest first. A document deleted with its subtree is one item; restoring it restores the subtree.
Permanently deletes everything in a workspace's trash. Cannot be undone.
Records an attachment whose bytes are already stored under their SHA-256 (the Blob port locally, an upload URL when hosted). Several attachments may share the same bytes.
Moves an attachment to the trash, where it can be restored.
Permanently deletes an attachment in the trash. Its bytes are removed when no other attachment uses them. Cannot be undone.
Lists a workspace's attachments, or one document's, newest first.

commands.summary: Leave a note or a comment
commands.description: Starts a thread beside a document; the body is not changed and threads are never published. A note is what the next reader should know about the text (why it says this, what it was checked against); a comment needs an answer. `quote` attaches it to a passage of the document; add `prefix` or `suffix` (the text just before or after) when the passage occurs more than once. Without `quote` it is about the whole page.

flags.name: kind
flags.description: note: context for the next reader, kept quietly beside the text. comment: expects an answer.

flags.name: exact
flags.description: For editors: quote is the document's text already, store it as given.

flags.name: id
flags.description: Client-minted id of the reply. Generated when omitted.

commands.summary: Edit a thread or a reply
commands.description: Changes the text of a thread or of one reply. Only its author may.
Attaches a thread to another passage, or to the page as a whole with anchor null. Editors use it to keep a thread on its text while the text is edited.
Marks a thread as dealt with: an answered comment, a note that no longer applies. It is kept, and resolved: false reopens it.

commands.summary: Delete a thread or a reply
commands.description: Deleting a thread hides its replies too. Undo with thread.restore.

commands.summary: Restore a thread or a reply

commands.description: The notes and comments left beside a document, oldest first, each with its replies. Open threads only unless `state` says otherwise.

flags.name: kind
flags.description: note: context for the next reader, kept quietly beside the text. comment: expects an answer.

commands.description: Lists sessions that changed a workspace, most recent first.
Lists every operation a session applied, oldest first.
Reverts every change a session made, newest first, as one undoable step. Changes that later edits by others touched are skipped and reported, as are changes that cannot be undone.

Lists what happened in a workspace, most recent first: documents created, renamed, moved, edited, deleted; files added; database changes; on a hosted workspace also members, teamspaces, sharing, API tokens and publishing. Repeated changes to the same thing by the same actor within a few minutes are one item with a count. Page with `cursor`.

flags.name: cursor
flags.description: nextCursor of the previous page. Pass the same filters.

flags.name: target-id
flags.description: Only changes to this document, file or database.

flags.name: search
flags.description: Only items whose title (or the name of the person, teamspace or token they are about) contains this (case-insensitive).

commands.description: Creates a database: a document whose children are its rows. With documentId, turns an existing document into a database (its children become rows). Starts with a title property and one view.

flags.name: id
flags.description: Client-minted id of the new database document.

flags.name: document-id
flags.description: Turn this existing document into a database.

flags.name: teamspace-id
flags.description: Hosted: the teamspace a new top-level database goes into (null: the creator's private section; absent: the workspace's default teamspace, which every member shares). Ignored with parentId or documentId, and in local mode.

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key (recorded so replays converge).

commands.description: Sets the filter applied to every view and the row templates.

commands.summary: Turn a database back into a page
commands.description: Removes the database (schema and views go to the trash with it); the document and its rows stay as ordinary pages. To delete the document itself use doc.delete.

commands.summary: Replace a database's schema and views
commands.description: Applies a whole definition (what fromBase reads from a .base file): properties and views with a known id are updated, new ones created, live ones missing from it deleted. Row values are not touched.
Returns a database's settings, live properties and views, in order.
The database's row templates (config.templateIds), in order, live ones only. Templates are left out of views, counts and relation pickers; pass one as createRow's templateId.
Lists the live databases of a workspace (database documents not in the trash).

Returns one window of a view's rows (filtered, sorted, grouped), with the total and group counts. Pass viewId for a saved view, or view for an ad-hoc one (both: view overrides). Properties in filters, sorts and groups are named by id, key or name. Page with window (offset, limit; hasMore says whether rows remain). uniqueId values are numbers (shown as prefix-number, e.g. LYD-12); filters take 12 or "LYD-12".

flags.name: view-id
flags.description: A saved view's id or name.

flags.name: today
flags.description: The caller's local date for relative date filters. Default: the server's.

commands.description: Adds a property. key defaults to the name (the frontmatter key in a folder). A two-way relation also adds the synced property on the related database (config.relation.reversePropertyId is its id). A uniqueId (config.prefix, e.g. LYD) numbers the existing rows in creation order; its key may not be "id".

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key (recorded so replays converge).

commands.description: Changes the display name only; the frontmatter key and row values stay (use database.updateProperty with key to rename the key).
Replaces the property's configuration and/or its key. A new key moves every row's value to it (one undo step).
Changes the type and converts every row's value (see the conversion table in the docs). convert: false keeps the values as they are.

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key (recorded so replays converge).

commands.description: Moves the property to the trash. Row values stay in the documents' properties, so restoring it brings them back. Deleting one side of a two-way relation makes the other side one-way.

commands.summary: Rename or recolour a select option
commands.description: Rows store the option's name, so renaming rewrites the rows that use it (one undo step).
Removes the option and clears it from every row that uses it (one undo step).

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key (recorded so replays converge).

commands.description: Copies a view right after itself. The name defaults to “<name> copy”.

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Fractional index key; siblings sort by (sortKey, id).

commands.description: The first view opens by default (and is what a plain embed shows).

flags.name: sort-key
flags.description: Explicit fractional key (recorded so replays converge).

commands.description: Changes the view's type and/or replaces the given top-level config fields (filter, sorts, groupBy, subGroupBy, columns, limit, summaries, layout); fields not given stay.

Creates a row (a document under the database). Values implied by the view's filter and by the group (group/subGroup keys) are filled in, as in Notion; values override them. With templateId, the template's properties and body are copied first. uniqueId properties get the next number unless values gives one (12 or "LYD-12").

Sets property values on one or many rows in one step: rowIds with set/unset applies the same values to every row; updates gives each row its own. Values are checked against the property type; unknown select options are added. Relation changes update the two-way side. uniqueId values are positive whole numbers: pass 12 or "LYD-12".

flags.name: exact
flags.description: Write the values as given: no type checks, no new options, no two-way relation updates. Undo uses it to restore earlier values exactly.

flags.name: new-options
flags.description: Options this call adds (recorded by the client so replays mint the same ids).

commands.description: Places a row after/before another (the manual order every unsorted view shows) and, with group/subGroup and a grouped viewId, moves it to that group by setting the grouped property.

flags.name: from-group
flags.description: The group it was in (list-valued groups).

commands.description: Copies rows (title, values and body), each right after its original.

flags.name: ids
flags.description: Client-minted ids for the copies, in order.

commands.description: Moves rows to the trash (as doc.delete). Relations to them hide until restored.

Creates, updates and deletes rows in one step. A row without id is created; with id it is updated (title renames it); delete: true moves it to the trash. values are keyed by property id, frontmatter key or name; relation values are row ids; select values are option names (new names become options); uniqueId values are numbers (pass 12 or "LYD-12"; new rows get the next number). unset clears properties. markdown sets the row's page content.

Adds, changes and removes properties in one step. update can rename (name), change the type (values are converted), the frontmatter key or the config (options, relation, number format, formula expression). Removed properties keep their values in the rows.
Adds, changes and removes views in one step. config is merged into the view's config (filter, sorts, groupBy, columns, …; properties by id, key or name); see get_database for the current values.

Exports every page, database and attachment you can read as a zip of the folder format: Markdown files with frontmatter, a `.base` file per database, attachments and `.lydie/`. Unzipped, it opens as a vault in Lydie's local mode and in Obsidian. The trash is left out. Returns a link to download the zip.

Adds to the workspace's inbox, a top-level page named Inbox that is created when missing. Without a title the text is appended to the inbox as a list item (prefixed with `time`, e.g. 09:41, when given). With a title it becomes a page inside the inbox, with the text as its body and `url` as its `source` property. Needs only the inbox:write scope, so a capture-only token (a web clipper, an automation) cannot read or change anything else. Returns ids only, never content.

flags.name: time
flags.description: Local time of the capture (HH:mm), shown before an appended item.
